title: "Trait retrieval"
---

```{python}
from _lib import *
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
leaf = read("validation_leaf")
met = read("validation_metrics")
spm = read("validation_species")
plant = read("validation_plant")
```

How well do RTM estimates match direct measurements of the corresponding trait (see
[Models](models.qmd) for the mapping, e.g. PROSPECT Cm ↔ LMA, Cw ↔ EWT, Cab ↔ extracted
chlorophyll a+b)? Error bars are 90 % credible intervals. Only fresh leaves are shown here;
dried, pressed and ground samples are on [Sample state & protocol](a-state-protocol.qmd).

```{python}
def scatter_grid(df, est="q50", lo="q05", hi="q95", meas="measured", key="observation_id", title_note=""):
    runs = df[["run_id", "model", "errmodel", "rt", "data_use"]].drop_duplicates()
    traits = [t for t in TRAIT if t in set(df["trait"])]
    nc = min(3, len(traits)); nr = int(np.ceil(len(traits) / nc))
    fig = make_subplots(rows=nr, cols=nc, subplot_titles=[trait_label(t) for t in traits],
                        horizontal_spacing=0.08, vertical_spacing=0.14)
    for i, t in enumerate(traits):
        r, c = i // nc + 1, i % nc + 1
        g = df[df["trait"] == t]
        v = np.r_[g[meas], g[est]]
        v = v[np.isfinite(v) & (v > 0)]
        if len(v) == 0:
            continue
        lo_, hi_ = np.quantile(v, [0.002, 0.998])
        one_to_one(fig, lo_ / 1.2, hi_ * 1.2, r, c)
        for m in MODELS:
            h = g[g["model"] == m]
            if h.empty:
                continue
            fig.add_trace(go.Scattergl(
                x=h[meas], y=h[est], mode="markers", name=MODEL_LABEL[m], legendgroup=m, showlegend=(i == 0),
                marker=dict(color=MODEL_COLOR[m], size=7, symbol=MODEL_SYMBOL[m], line=dict(color=SURFACE, width=1)),
                error_y=dict(type="data", symmetric=False, array=h[hi] - h[est], arrayminus=h[est] - h[lo],
                             color=MODEL_COLOR[m], thickness=1, width=0),
                customdata=np.c_[h[key], h[lo], h[hi]],
                hovertemplate="%{customdata[0]}<br>measured %{x:.3g}<br>estimate %{y:.3g} [%{customdata[1]:.3g}, %{customdata[2]:.3g}]<extra>" + MODEL_LABEL[m] + "</extra>"),
                r, c)
        rng = [lo_ / 1.2, hi_ * 1.2]
        log_axis(fig, "x", rng, r, c, "measured")
        log_axis(fig, "y", rng, r, c, "RTM estimate")
    fig.update_layout(height=340 * nr + 60, margin=dict(t=110),
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.0, yanchor="bottom", yref="container"))
    return fig
```

## Leaves

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "RTM estimates vs measurements for individual fresh leaves (Hetero + OU error model, all measured quantities). Log axes; gray = 1:1."
if len(leaf):
    d = leaf[(leaf["sample_state"] == "fresh") & (leaf["errmodel"] == "ou") & ~leaf["rt"].astype(bool)
             & (leaf["data_use"] == "all") & ~leaf["relative"]]
    show(scatter_grid(d))
else:
    no_data()
```

```{python}
#| tbl-cap: "Retrieval metrics per run and trait, fresh leaves, all datasets pooled. r2_log/ccc on log scale; bias_log = mean log(estimate/measured); coverage90 = share of measurements inside the 90 % interval; crps_log = log-score."
if len(met):
    m = met[(met["group"] == "all") & (met["sample_state"] == "fresh")].assign(run=lambda d: d.apply(run_label, axis=1))
    cols = ["run", "trait", "n", "r2_log", "spearman", "ccc", "bias_log", "slope_log", "nrmse", "coverage90", "crps_log"]
    show_table(fmt(m[[c for c in cols if c in m]]))
```

## Species means

Species means use leaves that have both a measurement and an estimate. The posterior
uncertainty of the estimates is propagated draw by draw into the species mean.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Species-mean RTM estimates vs species-mean measurements (≥ 3 leaves per species). Hetero + OU error model."
if len(spm):
    d = spm[(spm["errmodel"] == "ou") & ~spm["rt"].astype(bool) & (spm["data_use"] == "all")]
    d = d[d["trait"].isin(TRAIT)]
    if len(d):
        show(scatter_grid(d, key="species_id"))
```

```{python}
#| tbl-cap: "Species-mean retrieval: Pearson R² (log) and Spearman correlation across species."
if len(spm):
    rows = []
    for (rid, t), g in spm.groupby(["run_id", "trait"]):
        ok = (g["q50"] > 0) & (g["measured"] > 0)
        if ok.sum() >= 5:
            rows.append({"run_id": rid, "trait": t, "n_species": int(ok.sum()),
                         "r2_log": np.corrcoef(np.log(g.loc[ok, "q50"]), np.log(g.loc[ok, "measured"]))[0, 1] ** 2,
                         "spearman": g.loc[ok, "q50"].corr(g.loc[ok, "measured"], method="spearman")})
    show_table(fmt(pd.DataFrame(rows)))
```

## Pooled-sample (plant-level) traits

Some traits were measured on a pooled sample of several leaves; LOPEX pigments and chemistry
are an example. These are compared with the mean of the RTM estimates over those leaves.

```{python}
if len(plant):
    show_table(fmt(plant))
else:
    print("No plant-level comparisons in this fit set.")
```

## Suspect groups

Sometimes most leaves of one dataset and year miss their measured trait by a similar factor.
That points to the measurements (units, method) or to that group's spectra rather than to the
RTM. Each (dataset, year, trait) group is compared with the same trait in all other groups:
the ratio of its median log(estimate / measured) to theirs (`deviation_ratio`). Comparing
with the other groups means a bias shared by a trait everywhere is not blamed on one dataset.

A group is flagged when, in at least half of the runs estimating the trait, it has at least
3 leaves and deviates by more than a factor of 1.5 either way. The thresholds are in
`config/config.yaml` (`analysis.flag`).

Flagged groups are not excluded automatically. To exclude a group, add it to
`analysis.exclude` with a reason, or set `analysis.auto_exclude_flagged`; see
[Best trait estimates](b-best.qmd).

```{python}
#| tbl-cap: "(Dataset, year, trait) groups, flagged first. median_ratio: median estimate / measured; deviation_ratio: the same relative to the trait's ratio in other groups (1 = typical); share_runs_flagged: share of runs in which the group deviates by more than the threshold."
sus = read("suspect_groups")
if len(sus):
    show_table(fmt(sus))
else:
    no_data()
```
